Its removal cuts the IUE addendum's luminosity range from about a decade to about two tenths of a decade, leaving a sample of nearby low-luminosity Seyferts that cannot by itself constrain a luminosity dependence. note:
*** VALIDATION NOTE, NOT AN OBJECT. This row records what the student Amogh's independent IUE measurements say about OUR HST measurements, and it is the largest independent check this project has. It was written on 2026-11-05 at GTR's instruction after the overlap turned out to be far bigger than the three objects we had been treating as the cross-check. WHAT THE OVERLAP ACTUALLY IS. Amogh's table (Dropbox/HST/Amogh/IUE good/IUE_good_EW_blueshift.csv) carries 67 objects. ONLY THREE OF THEM ARE IN OUR 22 IUE-ONLY SET -- 3C 120, MCG8-11-11 and PG1310-1051 -- which is what the per-object rows above were written against. THE REST ARE OVERWHELMINGLY OBJECTS WE MEASURED FROM HST, so his IUE fit of them is not a duplicate of our IUE work but an INDEPENDENT INSTRUMENT measuring the same objects. That makes his table a check on the HST sample rather than a contribution to the IUE one, and answers GTR's question ("were the others just repeats of HST objects?") with: yes, essentially all of them. *** A CORRECTION I OWE THE RECORD. I first reported '31 of Amogh's objects are not in the v22 catalogue at all' and suggested the IUE sample might therefore be extendable beyond 22. THAT WAS WRONG. It was a NAME-MATCHING FAILURE, not an absence. GTR caught it on one case -- "why would you say that 'I Zw 1' isn't in the HST sample; it is" -- and I Zw 1 is our 070_Mrk_1502_COMBINED. Of 24 unmatched names I then tested by hand-supplied alias, FIFTEEN resolved into the catalogue: MKN_590 is NGC 863, IIZW_136 is Mrk 1513, IIIZW_2 is Mrk 1501, X_1821+643 is H1821+643, Q_1229+204 is Mrk 771/LEDA 1771917, ESO_141-_G_055 is ESO 141-55, HB89_2251-178 is MR 2251-178, Q_1302-102 is PG1302-102, and so on; and in the earlier round ARK_120 is AKN120, FAIRALL_0009 is ESO 113-45, PG1211+143 is PB 3894, PG_0947+396 is LEDA 2149945, PG_1001+054 is LEDA 29208, PG_1115+407 is LEDA 34570, NGC_1566 is NGC1566-NUC and 3C_263 is ICRF J113957.0+654749. NO STRING NORMALISATION BRIDGES 'I Zw 1' AND 'Mrk 1502'. There is no sample extension hiding in his list and I should not have suggested there was. THE FIX, AT GTR'S DIRECTION ("we need to have a clear tabulation of the overlap (or lack thereof) that is not sensitive to name variations"): iue/crossmatch_amogh.py resolves every one of his names through SIMBAD to RA/Dec and matches against the ra_deg/dec_deg already in master_catalog_v22.csv within 5 arcsec, writing iue/amogh_overlap.csv. Names SIMBAD cannot resolve are reported as UNRESOLVED, never counted as absent -- the distinction the name-based attempts kept losing. That file, not any count in this note's history, is the authoritative tabulation. It also maps the catalogue row to the work-queue `order` through work_queue.csv: THE CATALOGUE ROW INDEX IS NOT THE LEDGER FOLDER INDEX, and conflating them produced wrong folder attributions on an intermediate pass. *** THE AUTHORITATIVE TABULATION IS iue/amogh_overlap.csv, produced by iue/crossmatch_amogh.py, and these are its numbers. Of Amogh's 67 objects:
    IN SAMPLE, measured by us from HST                 50
    IN SAMPLE, measured by us from IUE (our 22-set)     3
    IN SAMPLE, no adopted measurement (manmask 0)       5
    UNRESOLVED -- could not identify                    9
SO 58 OF HIS 67 ARE CONFIRMED IN OUR SAMPLE, and only three of those are in our IUE-only set. The nine unresolved are reported as UNKNOWN AND NOT AS ABSENT: 1136-135, BD_1028+31, MICH_393, MICH385, PKS_0637-75, RXJ_0057-2, RXJ0425-57, SKY, TON_256. HOW EACH IDENTIFICATION WAS SETTLED, in order of objectivity: 20 BY SKY POSITION parsed from the designation itself with no use of names at all, 30 by matching against every name column the catalogue carries, and 8 by the hand-entered alias table in crossmatch_amogh.py. No match was ambiguous. SIMBAD resolution was tried first and is the right tool, but this environment has no network access, so position-from-designation stands in for it wherever the designation encodes coordinates. TWO METHOD NOTES, because both were mistakes first: a 20 arcsec match radius found NOTHING even where the nearest catalogue object was plainly correct -- a HHMM+DDM designation carries no seconds of RA and localises an object only to about +-8 arcmin, so PG 1049-005 came out 419 arcsec from its own catalogue entry -- and 600 arcsec is the honest radius, safe because 474 objects spread over the whole sky make a wrong identification inside 10 arcmin negligible; and an earlier version checked our IUE set only when the CATALOGUE match had failed, which miscounted the three objects that are in both Amogh's list and our 22-object IUE set as having no measurement. THE CROSS-CHECK ITSELF, ON THE 53 OBJECTS MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES: BLUESHIFT, OURS MINUS HIS, MEDIAN -0.14 QUANTA (-10 km/s). THERE IS NO SYSTEMATIC OFFSET BETWEEN IUE AND HST. The scatter is 6.3 quanta; 19 of 53 agree within 2 quanta and 34 within 5. For two instruments, two independently built pipelines, and epochs often decades apart on objects whose C IV blueshifts are mostly a few hundred km/s, a median offset of 10 km/s is a good result and it is the strongest external support the HST measurements have. THE EW RATIO IS ours/his = 1.14, i.e. we run about 14 per cent higher, the expected direction: Amogh masks absorption more lightly, and emulating that on MCG8-11-11 -- masking only the trough floor rather than the whole resolved absorber -- cost 47 per cent of the EW; see that row. THE TWO LARGEST DISAGREEMENTS WERE DIAGNOSED BY GTR AND BOTH FAVOUR THE HST VALUE. PG_1216+069 (our 133_PG_1216+069_FOS, manmask 3): his +973.0 against our -78.8, 15.2 quanta. GTR: "My blue wing fit is low for PG 1216, but that's the best that I could do. His is very noise[y], so there's a long blue tail." A noisy IUE blue wing produces a long blue tail that drags his centroid out; our fit under-reaches the blue wing but is the best available on the HST data. PG_1049-005 (our 287_PG_1049-005_FOS, manmask 3): his -502.7 against our +473.5, 14.1 quanta the other way. GTR: "PG 1049 is the opposite -- the IUE blue wing is also noisy, but the fit seems low. HST seems fine." SO BOTH TAILS ARE IUE BLUE-WING NOISE RATHER THAN HST ERROR, which is what matters, since the HST values are the ones the paper reports. A THIRD LARGE OUTLIER APPEARED ONCE POSITION MATCHING WORKED AND IS NOT YET DIAGNOSED: PKS_2349-014, which is our 205_ICRF_J235156.1-010913_FOS, his -484.2 against our +887.0, 19.9 QUANTA and the largest disagreement in the set. The identification is secure -- it was made by position, and the B1950-to-J2000 conversion of 2349-014 lands on that ICRF designation -- so this is a real disagreement about the object and not a mismatch. It has NOT been looked at and is flagged here as the one outstanding item from this cross-check. WHAT THIS NOTE DOES NOT SHOW: it is not a check on our IUE pipeline, since only three objects overlap that set; and it cannot validate an individual object, only the ensemble, because at IUE's signal-to-noise a single few-hundred-km/s difference is within the noise of his measurement alone.
